name: Mezzotint
summary: An intaglio tone process: a rocker roughens the whole plate to a black, and the engraver scrapes and burnishes the lights.
how: Rock the plate in 20–40 directions with a curved, toothed rocker until it prints a full, even black.
Scrape and burnish the grain flat where the image needs light; a full burnish prints white.
Work from dark to light, and check the tone with proofs at each stage.
Print only 50–100 good impressions; the soft grain wears quickly.

origin.note: Ludwig von Siegen makes a portrait of Amalia Elisabeth, Landgravine of Hesse-Kassel in the new tone process.

adoptions.via: London engravers such as John Raphael Smith and Valentine Green reproduce the portraits of Reynolds and Gainsborough, and Europe calls it the English manner.
